events.title: Baldwin III takes sole control of Jerusalem from his mother Melisende
events.description: After besieging Queen Melisende in the Tower of David, Baldwin III had become master of Jerusalem by this date, and she retired to Nablus under a negotiated settlement. He began his sole rule by giving the government offices to his trusted partisans.

events.title: Pope Boniface VIII founds the Sapienza University of Rome
events.description: By a decree of Pope Boniface VIII, the Sapienza was founded in Rome as a studium for ecclesiastical studies, under more control than the free-standing universities of Bologna and Padua. Pope Eugene IV completely reorganised the studium in 1431.

events.title: The Mamluks defeat the Ilkhanate at Marj al-Saffar
events.description: Near Kiswe, south of Damascus, the Bahri Mamluks of Egypt met the Mongols of the Ilkhanate and their Armenian allies in a battle lasting until 22 April. The battle, a disastrous defeat for the Mongols, ended their invasions of the Levant.

events.title: Jacques Cartier sails from Saint-Malo for North America
events.description: Jacques Cartier left Brittany on the first of three voyages that explored the Gulf of St Lawrence. His expeditions laid the basis for France's later claim to Canada.
events.html: Jacques Cartier left Brittany on the first of three voyages that explored the Gulf of St Lawrence. His expeditions laid the basis for France's later claim to Canada.

events.title: Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada's conquistadors take Bacatá
events.description: Spanish conquistadors led by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada subjected Bacatá, the main settlement of a Muisca confederation and seat of the zipa, ruler of the Bogotá savanna. The name of Colombia's capital, Bogotá, is derived from Bacatá.

events.title: Oliver Cromwell dissolves the Rump Parliament
events.description: Cromwell entered the Commons with musketeers and expelled the remaining members. The act led to his rule as Lord Protector later that year.

events.title: Robert Blake destroys a Spanish fleet at Santa Cruz de Tenerife
events.description: Admiral Robert Blake sailed into the defended harbour and burned the Spanish ships sheltering there without losing a vessel of his own. It was one of the boldest naval actions of the age.
events.html: Admiral Robert Blake sailed into the defended harbour and burned the Spanish ships sheltering there without losing a vessel of his own. It was one of the boldest naval actions of the age.

events.title: Alaungpaya's men wipe out a Hanthawaddy detachment at Halin
events.description: Alaungpaya led forty of his best men against a 50-man Hanthawaddy detachment at Halin, south of Shwebo, and wiped it out, in the first resistance of the Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War. The war ended the Mon people's centuries-long dominance of the south.

events.title: France declares war on Austria
events.description: The Legislative Assembly voted for war against the Habsburg monarch, opening the French Revolutionary Wars. Conflict between France and the European powers would last, almost unbroken, until 1815.

events.title: Two students kill 13 people at Columbine High School
events.description: Two students at the Colorado school shot dead twelve classmates and a teacher before killing themselves. The attack transformed school security and police response tactics across the United States.
events.html: Two students at the Colorado school shot dead twelve classmates and a teacher before killing themselves. The attack transformed school security and police response tactics across the United States.

song: Tamil Shaivas, devotees of Shiva in South India
Hymns to the god Shiva by three Tamil poet-saints who lived some 1,300 years ago; they are still sung every day in temples of Tamil Nadu.
